narrative_purpose: Shows rugosity as the driver of life: a complex three-dimensional reef holds far more organisms than a flattened one of the same footprint.
subject: A continuous seascape contrasting two reef states. On the left, a tall, intricately branched and folded reef riddled with caves, arches and overhangs, dense with small fish, invertebrates and shelter-seeking creatures packed into every crevice. On the right, the same footprint reduced to a low, smooth slope of grey coral rubble with almost no structure and only a few scattered organisms drifting over it.
scene: One reef floor in clear shallow water transitioning from complex left to flattened right, no hard border.
camera: Wide straight-on plate at reef scale, both states at equal footprint width.
light: Cyan glow through the complex crevices on the left, flat dull light over the bare rubble on the right, indigo in the deep caves.
palette: Ocean teal and cyan on the living complex side, muted stone-grey on the flattened side, void indigo cave shadows.
style: Painterly naturalist comparison plate, organic, not an infographic.
detail_level: Crisp on the crevices and sheltering fauna at left and the bare rubble at right; open water above for callouts.
composition: Complex-left / flat-right across the frame with open low-detail water band above for labels on rugosity and lost habitat.
consistency_notes: Same reef footprint both sides; the difference is structural complexity, not species. Keep palette consistent with earlier reef figures.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no panel dividers, no photographic or 3D-render look, no cartoon style
